comments.body:
## How Cloud's readers actually page (established from the code, not assumed)

All three readers in adapters/jira/acli_graph.py (get_parent_map, get_comment_map,
get_issuelinks_map) drive POST /rest/api/3/search/jql with an OPAQUE cursor:
the request body carries {jql, maxResults: 100, fields: [<one field>]}, plus
nextPageToken echoed back from the previous response. Termination is
"if resp.get('isLast'): break" then "if not next_page_token: break".

This is structurally DIFFERENT from the DC bug family. DC advanced an integer offset by
the REQUESTED page size, so a server that capped pages below the request (a lowered
jira.search.views.default.max) made a short first page read as "that is all there is".
Cloud never computes an offset; it hands back whatever token the server gave. So the
advance-by-requested-size arithmetic does not exist here to get wrong.

Measured on the branch before any test was written (stub over _direct_rest_post_json,
250 issues):
  * 250 seeded at 100/page -> 250 recovered in 3 requests, cursors sent
    [None, cursor:100, cursor:200]
  * pages capped at 40 while 100 requested (the DC-shaped short-page server)
    -> 250 recovered in 7 requests; a SHORT page does NOT stop the walk
  * final page with no isLast and no token -> 250 recovered in 3 requests

So Cloud pages CORRECTLY today. Per the ticket's own framing, the deliverable is
therefore a net that would CATCH a regression, not a bug report -- with one exception
recorded below.

## Seeding, and why

250 items at 100/page = THREE pages. Two pages can pass a fencepost error by accident;
three cannot. _SEEDED_ISSUES=250, _EXPECTED_PAGE_SIZE=100, _EXPECTED_PAGES=3 are
module-local LITERALS, deliberately not imported from the reader's own page_size -- an
expectation derived from the constant under test moves with the bug and can never fail.
The short-page variant seeds the same 250 against a 40-item server cap = 7 pages.
Assertions are on the recovered SET (plus payload identity spot-checks at index 0, 105
and 249), not on a count, so a reader returning the right NUMBER of wrong items fails.

## New test module

tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py (521 lines, new file;
adapters/jira/acli_graph.py unchanged at 606 lines -- NO production change in this
change). 27 passed + 1 xfailed. Sits beside the DC equivalent
test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py for parity.

AC coverage:
  * AC1 recovered set + payload identity across 3 pages, per reader
  * AC2 cursor advance asserted on the recorded request BODIES: request 0 must carry NO
    token; request N must equal the token response N-1 returned; no token re-sent
  * AC3 both stop conditions in ISOLATION -- isLast alone (the final page deliberately
    still offers a live token, so a token-only reader would spin) and an exhausted cursor
    alone (no isLast; both the absent-token and explicit-null spellings)
  * AC4 strict xfail, see the defect section below
  * AC5 mutation ledger below
  * AC6 an AST guard over adapters/jira/*.py: any function POSTing to
    /rest/api/3/search/jql must both loop and mention nextPageToken. DC's guard scans the
    DC transport source only, so this seam was open on Cloud; both together close the
    class on EITHER deployment. The guard shares its predicate with a teeth test driving
    a synthetic offender (with a paginated reader and a non-search POST as negative
    controls) and with a coverage test that fails if the scan ever goes vacuous.

comments.body:
## Mutation ledger (AC5) -- every oracle proven able to fail

Each mutation was applied to the real reader source (all three readers at once, since the
loop is hand-rolled three times), the targeted module re-run, then the file restored from
a byte-for-byte backup. No AttributeError / ImportError verdicts -- every RED below is an
AssertionError from an oracle, naming the truncation.

MUTATED: unconditional `break` at the end of the cursor loop (stop after page one, both
stop conditions and the advance removed).
FAILED: 18 tests. Exact messages included
  * test_reader_recovers_every_seeded_issue_across_three_pages[get_parent_map] --
    "get_parent_map recovered 100 of 250 issues -- the whole-project map is TRUNCATED, so
    issues past the first page look parentless / comment-less / link-less to the differ.
    Missing: ['DIG-100', 'DIG-101', ...]" (same for get_comment_map, get_issuelinks_map)
  * test_a_short_page_does_not_terminate_the_walk[get_parent_map] -- "get_parent_map
    recovered 40 of 250 against a server capping pages at 40: a SHORT page was mistaken
    for the LAST page"
  * test_an_exhausted_cursor_alone_terminates_the_walk[null-token-get_parent_map] --
    "get_parent_map/null-token recovered 100"
  * test_islast_alone_terminates_the_walk[get_parent_map] -- "recovered 100 of 250 --
    truncated before isLast"

MUTATED: `if resp.get("isLast") or len(issues) < page_size: break` -- the exact DC bug
(break on a SHORT page) transplanted into Cloud.
FAILED: 3 tests, test_a_short_page_does_not_terminate_the_walk[all three readers] --
"get_comment_map recovered 40 of 250 against a server capping pages at 40: a SHORT page
was mistaken for the LAST page". Note this mutation is invisible to every other oracle,
which is exactly why the short-page server variant is in the module.

MUTATED: never echo the cursor back (`if False: body["nextPageToken"] = ...`).
FAILED: 21 tests, including the dedicated cursor oracle
test_the_cursor_token_advances_across_requests[get_comment_map] -- "get_comment_map
request 1 carried cursor None but response 0 handed back 'cursor:100' -- the cursor did
not advance".

MUTATED: remove the null-cursor stop, leaving only `isLast`.
FAILED: exactly the 6 test_an_exhausted_cursor_alone_terminates_the_walk cases
(absent-token and null-token x 3 readers) -- "get_comment_map issued 26 requests for 3
pages: an exhausted (absent-token) cursor did NOT stop the walk -- it kept re-requesting,
which on a live server is an unbounded spin against Jira". No other oracle catches this,
which is the point of asserting the two stop conditions independently.

MUTATED: remove the `isLast` stop, leaving only the token check.
FAILED: 18 tests, including test_islast_alone_terminates_the_walk[get_parent_map] --
"get_parent_map kept paging past isLast: 26 requests" and
test_the_cursor_token_advances_across_requests -- "re-sent a cursor token:
['cursor:100', 'cursor:200', 'cursor:250', 'cursor:250', ...]".

MUTATED: add a FOURTH whole-project reader to acli_graph.py (get_status_map) that POSTs
/rest/api/3/search/jql once with no cursor loop -- the scenario AC6 exists to prevent.
FAILED: test_no_cloud_whole_project_reader_skips_the_cursor_loop -- "function(s) in
adapters/jira POST /rest/api/3/search/jql without a nextPageToken cursor loop and will
silently return only the FIRST page: ['acli_graph.py:get_status_map (line 475)']".

MUTATED: drift the guard's own file glob from "*.py" to "*.pyx" (i.e. the guard scans
nothing and passes vacuously -- the failure mode that lets a structural guard rot).
FAILED: test_the_structural_guard_actually_sees_the_three_known_readers -- "the guard's
own source list does not include acli_graph.py -- it scanned [], so the whole guard is
VACUOUS". Note the guard test itself stays GREEN under this mutation, which is why the
coverage teeth test exists.

### Note on hang-proofing, which is load-bearing here

Two of the mutations above (drop either stop condition) make the reader re-request the
same offset FOREVER on a live server; the mutant would hang the suite rather than fail.
The fake server therefore raises after 25 requests with "the walk never terminated: N
requests for M issues -- the cursor loop is spinning". The readers' fail-open
`except Exception` converts that into their silent-partial-map path, which is precisely
what the recovered-set and request-count oracles then report -- so the mutation surfaces
as a named RED instead of a timeout. That same fail-open swallow is the second-order
effect described in the defect ticket below.

### Existing assertions

None weakened. The prior single-page coverage in
mutate/test_acli_cross_mixin_binding.py:188,200 is untouched and still passes (52 passed
across the new module + that module + the DC pagination module).

## A REAL Cloud defect was found by AC4 -- filed, not fixed here

[rebar:cabc-7a98-d173-4d7c] "Cloud acli_graph readers spin forever on a repeated cursor
token", linked discovered_from this ticket.

Mechanism: if the server returns the SAME non-null nextPageToken with isLast falsy, the
request body is byte-identical each iteration, the response is identical, and neither
break fires -- the loop never terminates. There is no same-token-twice guard and no
request ceiling. fetcher._iter_pages HAS exactly this guard (fetcher.py:286-308,
token_seen_count -> SilentTruncationError(reason="same-token-twice")); these three readers
are a separate code path with a separate cursor and do not.

Second-order effect: each reader wraps the POST in a fail-open `except Exception: break`,
so the spin ends only when the transport finally errors, and that error is swallowed at
WARNING -- the pass then completes with a SILENTLY PARTIAL map. Same invisible symptom as
change 1105 / [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] / [rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd].

Measured: 26 requests issued against a token-repeating stub, ending only because the test
harness raised at its own 25-call cap; the result was a 1-entry map. Without the harness
cap the call does not return.

Per this ticket's instructions, production behaviour was NOT changed. AC4's oracle is
therefore committed as the CONTRACT (the reader must stop on its own within two requests,
without the harness breaking the spin) under xfail(strict=True) citing the bug id:
test_a_repeated_cursor_token_stops_the_walk_on_its_own. strict=True means it goes RED the
moment the guard lands, forcing conversion to a plain assertion -- so the xfail cannot rot
into permanent silence. AC4's "pins which" is answered explicitly: today it does NEITHER
(no raise, no stop); the pin is on the correct behaviour plus the filed defect.

## Gates

  * module sizes: acli_graph.py 606 -> 606 (unchanged; no production edit landed);
    new test module 521 lines. Nothing near the 800 cap.
  * ruff check + ruff format --check + mypy clean; pre-commit gate passed on commit.
  * docs/env-vars.md not affected (no env reads added).
  * targeted runs only: the new module, mutate/test_acli_cross_mixin_binding.py, and
    test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py -- 52 passed, 1 xfailed.
  * files touched: exactly one new test file. adapters/jira/** read-only.

compiled_state.description:
# Cloud's three whole-project readers have NO multi-page test — the same class fixed three times on DC

## Claim

`adapters/jira/acli_graph.py`'s `get_parent_map`, `get_comment_map` and `get_issuelinks_map` each
paginate a whole project through an opaque `nextPageToken` cursor at `page_size = 100`. **No test
exercises more than ONE page.** The only coverage,
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_acli_cross_mixin_binding.py:188,200`, feeds payloads
carrying `"isLast": True` — a single page, terminating immediately.

This is the SAME defect class that shipped three times on the DC/shared side and was fixed each
time only after it was found in production-shaped code:
  * change 1105 — `get_parent_map` advanced by the REQUESTED page size and stopped on a short page;
  * [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] — `get_issuelinks_map` and `get_comment_map`, the same bug;
  * [rebar:deac-4f5a-856a-49bd] — `fetcher._iter_pages`, which lost 92% of a snapshot when measured.
The Cloud copies of these three readers have never been tested past their first page.

## Why the risk is real rather than theoretical

* The cursor contract is genuinely stateful: `acli_graph.py:271-272` terminates on `isLast` OR on a
  null/absent `nextPageToken`, and the request echoes the token back at `:225`. Nothing asserts the
  cursor ADVANCES, that a second page is fetched and merged, that a null token stops the loop, or
  that a repeated token cannot spin forever.
* A silent truncation here is invisible: these are whole-project READS feeding the differ, so the
  symptom is missing parents / comments / links, not an error.
* DC now has exactly these tests (`test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py:66-128`, recovering 250
  items from a 20-cap client) plus a structural AST guard at `:166`. **That guard scans the DC
  transport source only**, so a fourth unpaginated caller cannot be added silently on DC and CAN be
  on Cloud.
* Live coverage does not compensate: the live Cloud tier exercises a real project, but nothing pins
  the working set above 100 issues, so a passing live run is not evidence the cursor loops.

NOTE the fetcher-level guard is NOT this. `fetch/test_fetcher_truncation_gate.py` covers the
FETCHER's search loop (same-token-twice / offset-stall). These three `acli_graph` readers are a
separate code path with a separate cursor.

## Provenance

Found by a Cloud-vs-DC test-parity audit commissioned while closing epic e369, not by a failure.
The audit's framing is worth keeping: the DC side has been heavily tested recently, so the parity
gap runs in BOTH directions — this is the largest instance of Cloud lacking what DC now has.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a test drives each of `get_parent_map`, `get_comment_map`, `get_issuelinks_map` against a
      fake ACLI client whose working set EXCEEDS one page, and asserts EVERY item is recovered —
      a count comparison against the seeded set, not a `> 0` floor
- [ ] the cursor is asserted to ADVANCE: the second request carries the token the first response
      returned, asserted on the recorded request bodies
- [ ] termination is asserted on BOTH documented conditions independently — `isLast: True`, and a
      null/absent `nextPageToken`
- [ ] a repeated cursor token does NOT loop forever (mirrors the fetcher's same-token-twice guard);
      it either raises or stops, and the test pins which
- [ ] each new test is MUTATION-CHECKED: breaking the loop after the first page must turn it RED,
      recorded on this ticket with the verdicts
- [ ] the structural anti-regression guard is extended to cover `adapters/jira/acli_graph.py`, so a
      fourth unpaginated whole-project reader cannot be added silently on EITHER deployment
compiled_state.title: Cloud whole-project readers (parent/comment/issuelinks maps) have no multi-page test
